newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-SWISS REFEREE APPEALS AGAINST LIFE BAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWISS REFEREE APPEALS AGAINST LIFE BAN.

text.p: Swiss referee Kurt Roethlisberger, who was suspended for life for attempted bribery last week, has appealed against the ban, a UEFA official said on Wednesday.
The date and venue for the appeal have not been determined.

Roethlisberger, once recognised as one of the game's top officials, was suspended last Thursday after a UEFA investigation found he solicited a bribe to fix a European Champions' League match between Grasshopper of Zurich and French champions Auxerre on October 30. Grasshopper won the match 3-1.
According to UEFA, Roethlisberger had approached Grasshopper manager Erich Vogel inquiring if he might be interested in having the match referee favour the Zurich club.
Roethlisberger, UEFA allege, told Vogel he was friendly with the referee and that it would be easy to arrange for 100,000 Swiss francs ($68,000).
Roethlisberger, who officiated at the 1990 and 1994 World Cups and the 1988 Seoul Olympics during his 27-year-career, has steadfastly maintained his innocence.
In a statement made on Monday through his lawyer Peter Treyer, the 46-year-old schoolteacher denied any wrong-doing.
Roethlisberger claimed the allegations stemmed from an informal talk between him and Vogel and never broached, in any way, the subject of fixing the match.
Roethlisberger added he was surprised to learn the Grasshopper club had brought the case to UEFA.
He has indicated he would defend himself by revealing damning details about soccer, blowing the lid off what could be a Pandora's box of deceit, corruption and bribery.
"In my 12 years of international (refereeing) I have seen and heard a lot but kept quiet out of loyalty to UEFA," he said without elaborating.
